title: Integrality of a finite-type scheme near a prime localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be prime, and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X_{\mathfrak p}=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $X_{\mathfrak p}$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], then there exists $a\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that $X_a=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}R[1/a]$ is integral [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. No separatedness, excellence, flatness, or domain hypothesis on $R$ is required.

source.place: Tag 01ON, lemma-characterize-integral, with its preceding affine-cover criteria: agent-formulated Noetherian localization consequence, not a verbatim assertion of that tag. The finite affine kernel argument is recorded in report.md; this fills the integrality detail in the spreading paragraph of Kurano–Shimomoto Lemma 4.4.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], choose a finite affine open covering $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ of $X$ with each $B_i$ a finite type $R$-algebra. Each $B_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Write $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $C_i=S^{-1}B_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso], the inverse images of the $U_i$ on $X_{\mathfrak p}$ and $X_b$ are affine opens with rings $R_{\mathfrak p}\otimes_R B_i$ and $R[1/b]\otimes_R B_i$, respectively, for any $b\notin\mathfrak p$. These opens cover because their underlying sets are inverse images of a covering.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Schemes Tags 01I4 and 01JR, affine base-change charts

proof.text: The tensor rings in Step 1 are $C_i$ and $B_i[1/b]$. Explicitly the first comparison sends $(r/s)\otimes x$ to $rx/s$; its inverse sends $x/s$ to $(1/s)\otimes x$. The second comparison has the same formulas with $s=b^n$. The fraction equality relations make these well defined: a relation killed by some denominator maps to zero since that denominator is invertible. On pure tensors and fractions both composites are the identity; the tensor balancing relation accounts for moving $r$ across. Thus these are ring isomorphisms compatible with the structural maps. Here $S^{-1}B_i$ means fractions with denominators from the image of $S$, using [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] on $B_i$ and its usual fraction multiplication.

source.place: Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, with the explicit universal-property localization specialization

proof.text: Let $K_i=\ker(B_i\to C_i)$. Since $B_i$ is Noetherian, [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] gives finitely many ideal generators $k_{it}$. The zero-fraction criterion in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives $s_{it}\in S$ with $s_{it}k_{it}=0$. Put $a=\prod_{i,t}s_{it}$, taking an empty product to be $1$. Primality of $\mathfrak p$ gives $a\notin\mathfrak p$. Each $s_{it}$ divides $a$, so $aK_i=0$ for every $i$. If $x/a^n$ maps to zero in $C_i$, its numerator lies in $K_i$, because $a$ maps to a unit there; then $ax=0$, hence $x/a^n=0$. Therefore every map $B_i[1/a]\to C_i$ is injective.

source.place: Elementary finite-generation argument from the definitions of Noetherian ring and localization

proof.text: Let $J$ consist of the indices for which $U_{i,\mathfrak p}$ is nonempty. For $i\in J$, integrality of $X_{\mathfrak p}$ gives that $C_i$ is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its subring $B_i[1/a]$ is a domain: an injective unital map into a nonzero domain forces $1\ne0$, and a zero product maps to a zero product. For $i\notin J$, $C_i=0$: sections on an empty open form the one-element ring by the sheaf axiom for the empty covering. The injection of Step 3 then forces $B_i[1/a]=0$, so $U_{i,a}$ is empty (the zero ring has no prime ideals). Thus the opens $U_{i,a}$ for $i\in J$ still cover $X_a$. Moreover $J$ is nonempty since $X_{\mathfrak p}$ is nonempty and is covered by the $U_{i,\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Tag 01ON, lemma-characterize-integral, and definition-integral: affine domain condition; elementary zero-ring cases

proof.text: The space $X_{\mathfrak p}$ is irreducible by [lem-pc-integral-scheme-irreducible]. Hence for any $i,j\in J$, its nonempty opens $U_{i,\mathfrak p}$ and $U_{j,\mathfrak p}$ meet: if they were disjoint, their closed complements would be two proper closed subsets covering the space, contrary to [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Since $a\notin\mathfrak p$, the fraction map $R[1/a]\to R_{\mathfrak p}$ gives a projection $X_{\mathfrak p}\to X_a$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. A point of that intersection maps into both $U_{i,a}$ and $U_{j,a}$, since their maps to $X$ are the same projections. Thus every pair $U_{i,a},U_{j,a}$ with $i,j\in J$ meets. No intersection of affine opens is assumed affine.

source.place: Tag 01OM, lemma-characterize-irreducible: nonempty opens of an irreducible space meet; pullback projection from the universal property

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-integral-affine-cover-criterion] to $Y=X_a$ and the covering indexed by $J$. Step 4 gives the nonempty index set and domain coordinate rings, and Step 5 gives all pairwise nonempty intersections. Therefore $X_a$ is integral, with $a\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ as required.
